summary.one_liner: A command-line tool for creating and managing a log of Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) as Markdown files in a project.
summary.what_it_does: The adr command initialises an ADR directory (default doc/adr, or a path you specify) and creates the first ADR recording the use of ADRs. It creates new numbered ADR files with a title and opens them in the editor named by the VISUAL or EDITOR environment variable. Using the -s option, a new ADR can be marked as superseding an earlier one, which also updates the old ADR's status to superseded. Built-in help is available through adr help. The README says the tool's own decisions are recorded as ADRs in its repository.
use_cases: recording architecture decisions in a project
creating numbered decision records in Markdown
keeping design decisions versioned alongside code
how_to_run: adr new Implement as Unix shell scripts
adr new -s 9 Use Rust for performance-critical functionality
notable: Creates numbered ADR Markdown files stored in your project repository
Supersedes option (-s) links new ADRs to old ones and updates the old status
Opens new records in your editor via VISUAL or EDITOR
Initialises the log with a first ADR based on Michael Nygard's article
caveats: The README does not state supported platforms or install steps beyond 'Install ADR Tools'
The README does not name a license
